question.text: Gulfstream Global Partners, a Singapore-tax-resident LP of a Cat II AIF, is about to claim India-Singapore treaty benefits on capital gains. The Multilateral Instrument (MLI) introduces a 'Principal Purpose Test' (PPT) into the treaty. What is the effect of the PPT?

answer.text: Treaty benefits are denied if obtaining the benefit was one of the principal purposes of the arrangement, unless granting the benefit is in accordance with the object and purpose of the treaty.
Treaty benefits are automatically available to all Singapore residents.
PPT only applies to dividend income, not to capital gains.
PPT replaces GAAR entirely — GAAR no longer applies once MLI is in force.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Principal Purpose Test, introduced through the OECD/BEPS Multilateral Instrument, is a general anti-abuse rule for tax treaties. It denies a treaty benefit (such as a favourable capital-gains article) if it is reasonable to conclude that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of an arrangement or transaction, unless granting the benefit in those circumstances is in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant treaty provisions. Where the PPT applies to a particular India treaty, even a tax-resident of the other contracting state must show genuine non-tax purpose and substance to access the treaty. The Trap: Treaty benefits are not automatic for all residents of the other state once an anti-abuse rule like the PPT is in place. The PPT is a general rule applicable to treaty benefits broadly, not limited to dividend income. It also does not eliminate the domestic General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR); the PPT and GAAR sit alongside each other rather than one replacing the other. Note: The cited workbook chapter discusses GAAR, the concept of a Limitation of Benefits clause and the MLI's signing/ratification timeline and its purpose of preventing inappropriate treaty benefits, but it does not spell out the PPT wording, its specific application to India-Singapore, or the position that the PPT acts as an overlay rather than a GAAR replacement. The framing above is general MLI / BEPS knowledge rather than a direct workbook citation.
